notes:
- Primary contact: Diego Alvarez (Head of Platform). Loves runtime performance; worried about long-term token run-rate.
- Use-case profile: high-throughput reranking for map tiles + small-chat assistant for first-response to field ops. Bursty, spiky traffic tied to weather events.
- Technical ask: want Dedicated for data isolation and predictable latency, but procurement balks at minimum commit (6 GPUs * 24/7).
- Price objection summary: finance ran model; with expected token volumes, per-token costs + GPU reserved run-rate push SaaS unit cost above current vendor (Vertex).
- Security: SRE flagged KMS integration and audit retention policy. Said they will require enterprise contract + SOC2/iso answers before approving any commit >$200k/yr.
- Internal org: no clear exec champion — platform team (Diego) is supportive but needs product to own budget signoff.
- Quote from Diego: "We can see the perf delta, but we simply can't sign a 12-month commit at this level today."
- AE notes: proposed 3-month pilot on hosted API with token caps + pre-agreed uplift to Dedicated if SLOs met. Finance asked for a forecast showing cost per MAU (sample workbook in drive).
- Current stance: quiet since procurement freeze; account unresponsive to pricing alternatives offered 2/10.
- Suggested playbook: build a short ROI model for 3 pilot scenarios (hosted burst, low-commit dedicated, private with smaller commit) and loop in solutions engineering to cost-optimize quantization/ batching.
- Risks: competitor price-matching, procurement timelines slipping, no champion.
- Good signals to reopen: exec sponsor identified, procurement releases capex hold, security completes KMS/audit OK.
short_summary: Mid-market geospatial customer enthusiastic about runtime but stalled on economics. Prefers Dedicated for latency/isolation; procurement freeze + high commit size + token run-rate make ARR not pencil. Proposed short pilot but account went quiet.
